reason: The cited evidence provides only partial support. E2 shows DSC can measure heat capacity and solidus in HEAs, supporting the DSC premise. E4 and E5 demonstrate 2NN MEAM MD can capture grain-size-dependent melting and short-range order in a specific refractory HEA, supporting the MD premise. However, no cited evidence supports the CALPHAD extrapolation premise for multicomponent HEAs (E1 is about rare-earth oxides, not HEAs), the claim that short-range order governs melting energetics is not directly evidenced, and the quantitative error margins are entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: CALPHAD can extrapolate binary/ternary interactions to predict multicomponent HEA phase energetics
2NN MEAM MD simulations can capture atomic-scale diffusion, phase change, and grain-boundary pre-melting in HEAs
DSC measurements can directly measure thermal properties (Cp, solidus) to calibrate simulations
Chemical short-range order governs phase energetics and structural rearrangements during melting
The combined approach can predict melting temperature within ±5% and fusion enthalpy/entropy within ±10%
